description: I’m an ECE student passionate about AI, electronics, software, spacecraft systems, digital circuits, and simulation. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I’m building ASTRAFORGE-X, an AI-powered spacecraft digital twin and mission engineering laboratory. I’m looking for teammates skilled or interested in AI/ML, coding, hardware, web development, space science, data analysis, UI/UX, simulation, visualization.
summary:
ASTRAFORGE-X is an AI-powered space mission engineering platform designed to explore spacecraft systems, mission operations, and intelligent fault analysis through an interactive digital twin simulation. It brings together Mission Control, Mission Designer, Spacecraft Cockpit, Space Weather visualization, subsystem monitoring, and What-If simulations in one unified environment.

The platform allows users to explore spacecraft subsystems, simulate potential failures, examine system behaviour, and access AI-assisted diagnostics and engineering recovery suggestions. By connecting mission visualization with interactive simulations, ASTRAFORGE-X demonstrates how intelligent software can support spacecraft engineering analysis and help users better understand complex mission scenarios.

The project aims to make space mission systems more accessible, improve understanding of spacecraft reliability, and demonstrate how AI-assisted decision support can contribute to future mission planning and fault-response workflows. It is an educational engineering simulation, not a real-time spacecraft control system.
details:
ASTRAFORGE-X: AI-Powered Space Mission Engineering and Intelligent Spacecraft Digital Twin

1. Project Overview

ASTRAFORGE-X is an AI-powered space mission engineering platform that provides an interactive environment for exploring spacecraft systems, mission operations, and intelligent fault analysis. It combines spacecraft digital twin concepts, mission visualization, simulation, and AI-assisted diagnostics into one platform.

2. How It Works

The platform provides multiple interactive modules:

  • Space Universe: Explore the space environment and mission-related visualizations.
  • Mission Control: View mission information and monitor simulated mission operations.
  • Mission Designer: Explore spacecraft mission design and configuration.
  • Spacecraft Cockpit: Interact with spacecraft subsystem visualizations.
  • What-If Simulations: Explore hypothetical subsystem failures and observe simulated system behaviour.
  • AI Diagnostics: Analyse simulated fault scenarios and receive AI-assisted explanations and engineering recovery suggestions.
  • Engineering Recovery Center: Explore possible responses to spacecraft subsystem issues.

Users can navigate between modules, examine system behaviour, simulate potential failures, and understand how intelligent decision-support systems can assist spacecraft engineering.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRAFORGE-X makes complex space mission engineering concepts easier to explore through an interactive digital environment. It supports learning about spacecraft subsystems, mission planning, system reliability, fault analysis, and engineering decision-making.

Its intended impact is to improve accessibility to space engineering concepts, encourage experimentation, and demonstrate how AI-assisted tools can support future spacecraft analysis and mission-planning workflows.

4. Technology and Tools Used

The project was developed as a web-based software platform using modern web technologies, including:

  • Next.js for application development and routing.
  • React for interactive user interfaces.
  • TypeScript for structured and maintainable code.
  • AI integration for intelligent diagnostics and engineering suggestions.
  • Vercel for application hosting and deployment.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and project development.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of ASTRAFORGE-X is the integration of spacecraft digital twin concepts, interactive mission modules, hypothetical failure simulations, and AI-assisted engineering recovery into a unified platform.

Instead of presenting space engineering concepts only through static information, the platform allows users to explore scenarios and interact with simulated spacecraft systems. The combination of visualization, simulation, and AI-assisted analysis creates an engaging approach to understanding complex engineering challenges.

6. Factors Considered During Development

The development focused on usability, accessibility, modular design, interactive learning, and clear presentation of spacecraft engineering concepts. The platform was designed to make its modules easy to navigate while presenting simulated system behaviour in an understandable way.

ASTRAFORGE-X is an educational engineering simulation and decision-support demonstration. It does not control real spacecraft or represent certified flight software, and its simulated outputs should not be interpreted as actual spacecraft telemetry.

Conclusion

ASTRAFORGE-X demonstrates how AI, interactive simulations, and digital twin concepts can make space mission engineering more accessible and engaging. It aims to inspire exploration, support engineering education, and showcase the potential of intelligent software in future space mission workflows.
